correctness.rationale: A complete facet H-description follows from the classical perfect-graph theorem, with independent facet witnesses. Each of the four possible pairwise facet types is classified by explicit dimension/codimension conditions; overlapping upper cliques differing in two or more parts cannot define ridges. Normal Gram products give the interior angles. Dirichlet integrals with Euclidean Jacobians sqrt(k), sqrt(k-1), sqrt(2k-1) give individual ridge Hausdorff measures, and exact combinatorial summation proves the three area totals. The five-partite equality follows symbolically from sin(2 arctan(1/2))=4/5 and gives V_{N-2} through the standard Steiner coefficient. The finite independent checker enumerates all facet pairs and exact ranks in 10 profiles; a separate SciPy convex-hull calculation checks every individual ridge area in four profiles, including two new two-nonsingleton five-partite cases.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete codimension-two Euclidean ridge-angle and intrinsic Hausdorff-measure invariant for the natural complete-multipartite stable-set polytopes with two or more nonsingleton parts. Its surprising dependence only on k and the singleton count after a single factorial volume scale is structural rather than a recomputed face count. The exact right-angle mean under nontrivial acute and obtuse ridge-area contributions for all K_{1,1,1,p,q}, p,q>=2, is a genuine geometric cancellation and gives a new exact V_{N-2}/V_N ratio; it is not implied by prior split-graph and bipartite metric claims.
